key_insight: A digital twin can evaluate local collective tariffs by combining household behavior, shared metering, and tariff logic in one simulation to show how aggregation affects community costs.
engineering_relevance: The method gives engineers a realistic way to test tariff designs for distribution-level energy systems before deployment, especially for communities with PV, batteries, and EV charging.
method: Agent-based modeling of household consumption and local generation
Virtual aggregation through a shared metering abstraction
Explicit tariff logic embedded in a unified simulation environment
evidence_signal: The abstract reports application to the Danish Local Collective Tariff across representative residential energy community scenarios, showing measurable community-level cost reductions and sensitivity to timing of load and generation.
watch_item: Results depend strongly on temporal alignment between consumption and generation, so cost neutrality across participants may not hold in all community configurations.
paper_title: A Digital Twin-Based Method for Evaluating Local Collective Tariffs in Distribution-Level Energy Systems
